text:
Daniel: Noticed an operational pattern: when we push heavy streaming workloads, we get connection storms from SDKs that attempt speculative hedging. This amplifies tail latency because ingress allocates resources evenly and long-lived streams block short ephemeral requests. Thinking out loud: introduce connection priority lanes + a drain-token handshake to enable safe preemption and steer hedging. Anyone experimented with similar?
Priya: Interesting. Can you sketch flows? How do we avoid breaking existing clients that do not support drain tokens?
Daniel: Sketch: 3 lanes per node: control (low-latency), short (ephemeral), stream (long-lived). New handshake header X-Redwood-Lane: control|short|stream. If unset, gateway infers lane from Content-Length and Connection semantics. Additionally, when stream lane needs to free up, we send a drain-token (HTTP 103 with header X-Resume-Token). Client can reconnect to the stream pool with that token — server preserves session metadata (idempotency key, last-ack).
Omar: How do we preserve side-effect guarantees across a token resume? If client retries, upstream might see duplicate events.
Li: Two ideas: 1) require idempotency-key for any stream message that triggers side-effects; 2) make resume token carry a monotonic cursor that tells upstream which events have been processed, so replays are bounded. For third-party clients, require conservative fallback: if no idempotency-key and we preempt, we mark request as non-resumable and return 410 to client.
Priya: I'm worried about hedging interactions. Clients that hedge might open multiple short/stream connections; if they all get routed to different lanes we lose usefulness of hedging. Maybe SDK should use lane-aware hedging: try short lane first with low timeout, then fallback to stream lane for persistent connection.
Daniel: Good point. We should update SDKs. For server-side, we can enforce fast-path reservation: reserve R slots in short lane per host and strict admission control so ephemeral requests never get head-of-lined by streams.
Omar: What about backpressure semantics? If a stream is preempted and the client resumes, the KV cache and KV pointers have to be consistent. How long do we keep resume state? Curious about memory blowup.
Li: Resume-token TTL is a knob. Keep minimal state: only the last-generation vector and pointer to cached chunks; evict oldest tokens LRU. We can also offload resume metadata to Redis with TTL and simple size caps. Prototype suggests ~200 bytes/token. At peak, with 100k concurrent resume-capable streams, that's 20MB, acceptable.
Priya: Config knobs proposal: per-route: lane_policy = {reserve_control: N, reserve_short: M, max_streams: S, preempt_threshold: p, resume_ttl: t}. Also add hedging_policy to discourage opening simultaneous stream+short lanes within a short window.
Daniel: Metrics to add: lane_utilization{control,short,stream}, preemption_count, resume_success_rate, resume_state_evictions, hedged_connections, short_p99_latency. Alerts: resume_success_rate < 90% OR short_p99 latency above baseline.
Omar: Rollout: 1) telemetry + lane inference only (no enforcement), 2) reserve a tiny short-lane pool on canaries, 3) add drain-token generation but only log actions, 4) enable soft-preempt with long resume_ttl, 5) SDK opt-in and enforce.
Priya: Also need an auth/binding check so a resume token can only be used by the same client (token bound to client fingerprint or API key) to avoid token theft.
Li: Wire example for 103 drain-token:
```http
HTTP/1.1 103 Early-Resume
X-Resume-Token: rsm_6b1f...
X-Resume-TTL: 30s
```
And client reconnect:
```http
POST /stream/connect
Authorization: Bearer <token>
X-Resume-Token: rsm_6b1f...
X-Redwood-Lane: stream
```
ci-bot: Canary rollout staged: lane-reservations enabled (5% hosts) in eu-central-1.
Daniel: Nice. Next steps: I'll write a short RFC with the lane model and the admission-control algorithm. Priya, can you own SDK guidance for hedging + lane headers? Omar, help size Redis store and eviction policy. Li, prototype drain-token generator and API.
Priya: Will prepare SDK doc and compat plan.
Omar: I'll simulate token memory under load and share numbers.
Li: Prototyping generator now, will post sample middleware.
Daniel: Thanks. We'll review RFC at next arch sync.
